findings.note: codex.go:81 guards the empty model id with an exact `model == CodexPrefix` comparison, but route() lowercases before matching (judge.go:114-119) and wireModel() strips the prefix case-insensitively (judge.go:168-172). A model of "CODEX/" or "Codex/" therefore routes to the CLI provider, passes validateCodex, and reaches the process as `-m ""`, surfacing as CodeJudgeTransport instead of the intended CodeJudgeModel. This is the same case-fold hole that TestCodexPrefixStrippingMatchesRouting (codex_test.go:164) was written to close in wireModel; the validator half was not updated, and the "empty model" case at codex_test.go:123 only exercises the exact-case form.

evidence.note: exact-case emptiness guard: `over || model == CodexPrefix`
route lowercases the model before prefix matching
empty-model case only covers the exact-case CodexPrefix

findings.note: codex.go:141-155 hand-rolls itoa with the comment "avoids pulling strconv in for two call sites", but package judge already imports fmt (judge.go:11) and uses fmt.Sprint for exactly this purpose (judge.go:653), so nothing is avoided. The hand-rolled loop is also wrong for math.MinInt: `n = -n` overflows back to a negative value, the `for n > 0` loop never runs, and the function returns a bare "-". Unreachable today because the only inputs are process exit codes, but it is 20 lines of duplicated stdlib carrying a latent formatting bug.

evidence.note: func itoa reimplements strconv.Itoa
n = -n overflows for math.MinInt, yielding "-"
fmt is already an import of the same package

findings.note: The codex arm has no retry ladder while the HTTP arm does. realJudge.Call loops to MaxAttempts with classified backoff (judge.go:528-548), but codexJudge.Call sets v.Attempts = 1 unconditionally and turns any non-zero exit into a fatal CodeJudgeTransport (codex.go:45, 62-63). A transient CLI failure (rate limit on the ChatGPT session, a network blip inside codex) therefore aborts the node where the equivalent HTTP judge would recover. The asymmetry may be deliberate, but neither the code comments nor the provider doc comment records it, so a reader comparing the two providers cannot tell intent from omission.

evidence.note: v.Attempts = 1, no retry loop
HTTP arm retries MaxAttempts with backoff

findings.note: parseCodexEvents assigns rather than accumulates token totals on `turn.completed` (codex.go:321-329), so if a stream ever carries more than one completed turn only the last turn's usage is reported. The HTTP arm accumulates across attempts with v.Tokens.Add (judge.go:534). This is the same class of under-reporting that TestCodexJudgeReportsTokensEvenWhenTheCallFails (codex_test.go:143) exists to prevent, and its stated stake is the same: understated spend weakens the budget convergence check. Low because `codex exec` normally emits a single turn.

evidence.note: tokens = run.TokenTotals{...} overwrites instead of adding
v.Tokens = v.Tokens.Add(tok) in the HTTP arm
